text:
Mattias Ekholm is 36, playing 21 minutes a night for Edmonton, and the Oilers are winning his minutes on the shot clock. At five on five they take about 55% of the shot attempts with him on the ice and fare more than six points better by expected goals (the quality of chances) than when he sits. That fits his profile: Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile among defensemen at driving his team's chance creation last season, worth 1.4 wins.

He has 3 goals and 11 points in 22 games, all at even strength, and he's been steady rather than spectacular, chipping in a point in six of his last ten. The Oilers have won seven of those ten.

The caution sign is luck. Our on-ice luck number for him is one of the biggest in the league: teammates and goalies have turned his shifts into far more goals for, and far fewer against, than the chances justified. His expected goal share is a coin-flip 51%. The puck play is real; the goal differential will likely come back toward it. Watch how Edmonton manages his minutes as the schedule piles up.
